events.text: {npc} is down on one knee on a floor made of cloud, {his} light guttering like a lamp in a draught. Every god who came to watch is very quiet. What happens next is yours to say.

choices.text: Let {him} go

effects.log: You step back and let {him} gather {his} light again.

choices.text: Leave {him} a wound the light will not close

effects.log: You make it quick, and you make it last a century.

choices.text: Crack {his} godhead

effects.log: You reach for the bright place at the centre of {him}.

choices.text: End it. This was to the death

effects.log: You do not look away.

choices.text: Hear the oath {he} offers

effects.log: {He} swears it by {his} own light, where every watching god can see.

events.text: {npc} tries to rise from the broken step of the sky and cannot. {He} looks up at you without asking for anything. A god asks nothing of another god, even now.

choices.text: Offer a hand. Then walk away

effects.log: You hold out a hand. {He} does not take it, and you go.

choices.text: Break the arm that held the light

effects.log: You take the arm, and you do not hurry.

choices.text: End {his} reign over anything, for good

effects.log: You kneel beside {him}, and {he} understands before you touch {him}.

choices.text: Finish what the duel began

effects.log: You do not look away.

choices.text: Take {his} oath instead

effects.log: {He} swears it by {his} own light, where every watching god can see.

events.text: The duel is over, and {npc} lies in the wreck of a small constellation, breathing hard. Lesser gods have gathered at a respectful distance. One of them says, quite clearly, "Finish it."

choices.text: Tell them it is finished

effects.log: You let your light go dim. The watchers are disappointed, and you do not care.

choices.text: Teach {him} a lesson {he} will feel for an age

effects.log: The watching gods go very quiet.

choices.text: Give the watchers what they asked for

effects.log: The watching gods go very quiet, and then they go away.

choices.text: Make sure {he} never comes back

effects.log: You do not look away.

choices.text: Let {him} swear it by {his} own light

effects.log: {He} swears it by {his} own light, where every watching god can see.

events.text: {npc} has stopped fighting. {He} sits against a pillar of the hall with {his} hands open and waits, the way a god waits who has lost and knows the old laws of heaven.

choices.text: By the old law: the loser walks

effects.log: You nod once and leave {him} the pillar.

choices.text: By your law: the loser limps for an age

effects.log: You decide the old law is too kind.

choices.text: By the hardest law: the loser never shines again

effects.log: You decide the old law is not kind enough.

effects.log: You do not look away.

effects.log: {He} swears it by {his} own light, where every watching god can see.

events.text: Starlight falls like rain on the field, and {npc} lies face down in it. {He} turns {his} head to look at you. "Well?" {he} says. "I would not have stopped."

choices.text: "I am not you"

effects.log: You leave {him} in the starlight.

choices.text: Make sure {he} remembers this night

effects.log: You make sure of it.

choices.text: Make sure {he} is never a danger again

effects.log: Two fingers on the light at {his} centre, and the stars go on falling.

effects.log: {He} swears it by {his} own light, where every watching god can see.

events.text: {npc} is waiting where two roads of the sky cross, as if you had an appointment. {He} burns brighter than when you last met. "I have thought about you every day of the last age," {he} says. "Every single day."

choices.text: Settle it here

ok.log: This time it ends the other way. {npc} goes down and stays down, and looks up at you with something new in {his} light.

fail.log: {npc} was ready for everything you did last time. {He} leaves you on the cloud road, and {he} is laughing.

choices.text: Talk {him} down from it

effects.log: It takes a whole season of the gods' slow talk. At the end of it {he} only looks tired, and goes back to {his} domain.

choices.text: Turn and take another road of the sky

effects.log: {He} lets you go. You hear {him} laugh behind you for a long way.

events.text: A message comes to your temple written in light on the inside of a bell: "The old field, at the dark of the moon. Come alone, or I will come to your worshippers." It is signed {npc}.

choices.text: Go, alone

ok.log: This time it ends the other way. {npc} goes down and stays down, and looks up at you with something new in {his} light.

fail.log: {npc} was ready for everything you did last time. {He} leaves you on the cloud road, and {he} is laughing.

choices.text: Go, and bring only words

effects.log: You talk on the old field until the moon comes back. {npc} leaves without fighting, which is the most {he} has ever given you.

choices.text: Let the bell ring itself quiet

effects.log: You let it ring. A month later every god in the hall has heard that you did not come.

events.text: {npc} walks into the hall where you are feasting and sits down across from you without asking. There is a new scar in {his} light and a new calm in {his} eyes, which is worse. "Finish your feast," {he} says. "Then we go outside."

choices.text: Finish the feast. Go outside

ok.log: This time it ends the other way. {npc} goes down and stays down, and looks up at you with something new in {his} light.

fail.log: {npc} was ready for everything you did last time. {He} leaves you on the cloud road, and {he} is laughing.

choices.text: Share the feast, and ask what {he} wants

effects.log: {He} wants to be seen. You see {him}, for a night, and it turns out to be enough.

choices.text: Leave by the back of the hall

effects.log: The servants of the hall do not even look up. Behind you, {npc} starts on your plate.

events.text: The heralds are talking about {npc}: a string of gods beaten since you last met, and every one of them, {he} tells anyone who listens, practice for you.

choices.text: Find {him} before {he} finds you

ok.log: This time it ends the other way. {npc} goes down and stays down, and looks up at you with something new in {his} light.

fail.log: {npc} was ready for everything you did last time. {He} leaves you on the cloud road, and {he} is laughing.

choices.text: Send word that you have nothing left to prove

effects.log: The answer comes back on the next wind: one word, "Fine." The heralds find something else to talk about.

choices.text: Let {him} talk

effects.log: You let {him} talk. The halls listen, and some of them believe {him}.

events.text: {npc} comes to find you with two heralds at {his} back. {He} is an elder god of the hall whose young one you broke, and {he} is not here to talk about it. "You know why I have come," {he} says.

choices.text: Answer {him} with your light

ok.log: {npc} goes down in front of the gods {he} brought to watch. {He} leaves without a word, and you know this is not over.

fail.log: {npc} puts you on the floor of heaven without hurrying. "That is all," {he} says. "We are even now." And for that hall, it seems, you are.

choices.text: Offer the hall a healer's offering and an apology

effects.log: You make the offering, and you bow, and it costs you more than the faith. {npc} takes both and goes.

choices.text: Bow low and ask the hall's pardon

effects.log: You bow until your crown almost touches the cloud. {npc} lets you stay there a long time before {he} leaves.

events.text: Word reaches your temple before {npc} does: the hall is sending someone. Then {he} is at your door, an elder god with old scars in {his} light and no patience. "Outside," {he} says.

choices.text: Go outside

ok.log: {npc} goes down in front of the gods {he} brought to watch. {He} leaves without a word, and you know this is not over.

fail.log: {npc} puts you on the floor of heaven without hurrying. "That is all," {he} says. "We are even now." And for that hall, it seems, you are.

choices.text: Send an offering to the hall first

effects.log: The offering arrives before you have finished talking. {npc} weighs it in one hand and nods.

choices.text: Shut the temple doors and wait for {him} to leave

effects.log: {He} leaves after a day and a night. Every god on the road saw {him} wait, and saw you not come out.

events.text: {npc} stands in the middle of the road of stars where every god can see, and calls your name, and the name of the one you hurt. An elder of that hall does not send letters.

choices.text: Walk out to meet {him}

ok.log: {npc} goes down in front of the gods {he} brought to watch. {He} leaves without a word, and you know this is not over.

fail.log: {npc} puts you on the floor of heaven without hurrying. "That is all," {he} says. "We are even now." And for that hall, it seems, you are.

choices.text: Pay the hall's price through a herald

effects.log: The herald is very good and very expensive, and by evening it is done.

choices.text: Leave the road of stars by a back way

effects.log: You leave by a back way. The road of stars remembers.

events.text: {npc} is older than most domains, and walks slowly, and every god on the road of stars steps aside without being asked. {He} is the elder of the one you beat at your door. "Twice," {he} says. "I will not need a third time."

choices.text: Face the elder

ok.log: The old god goes down on one knee and stays there, and the whole hall sees it. Nobody else from that hall will ever come looking for you.

fail.log: {npc} stops a finger of light a hair from your throat. "Enough," {he} says. "Now it is finished, for both halls." {He} goes, and it is.

choices.text: Kneel and offer the hall a great gift

effects.log: You kneel and the gift is carried in. {npc} looks at it for a long time and accepts.

choices.text: Kneel and offer nothing but your head bowed

effects.log: You kneel on the road of stars. {npc} lets you kneel until a star sets, and then {he} walks away.

events.text: The hall has stopped sending its elders. This time {npc} came, the eldest of them, and sat down in your temple's court to wait for you like a guest. "Sit," {he} says. "Then stand, and we will see."

choices.text: Stand, and see

ok.log: The old god goes down on one knee and stays there, and the whole hall sees it. Nobody else from that hall will ever come looking for you.

fail.log: {npc} stops a finger of light a hair from your throat. "Enough," {he} says. "Now it is finished, for both halls." {He} goes, and it is.

choices.text: Sit, and make the hall an offer

effects.log: You sit, and you talk, and the offer is large. {npc} takes your tea and the offer both.

choices.text: Sit, and say you are sorry

effects.log: You say it plainly. {npc} hears you out and leaves without a word, and every hall in heaven knows you said it.

events.text: Since the day your godhead cracked, the light will not gather; you sit to draw it in and nothing comes. Then a pilgrim who prays at every temple tells you of a healer-god in a forgotten domain who has mended worse. Maybe. Once.

choices.text: Go and find the healer-god

effects.log: You set out with what light you have. It is a long road across the sky, and you are slower on it than a god should be.

choices.text: Not yet

effects.log: You let the name go by. It will come round again.

events.text: An old sweeper of the hall, who has swept it since before your pantheon had a name, watches you pass and says without being asked, "Cracked at the centre. I know someone who mends that."

choices.text: Ask for the name

effects.log: The monk gives you a name and a direction, and goes back to sweeping.

choices.text: Thank the monk and go on

effects.log: You thank the monk. The name stays with you all the same.

events.text: The healer-god is real, and very small, and very rude. You can be mended, the healer says, but the price is not faith: a century of carrying starlight and grinding moon-root, and a flower from the edge of the Sealed Heavens that no young god will go near.

choices.text: Carry the starlight for a century

effects.log: A century of starlight and roots and silence. At the end of it the healer looks at you differently.

choices.text: Pay a bolder god to bring the flower

effects.log: A bolder god brings the flower back, and the healer grumbles that it is cheating, and takes it.

choices.text: Leave, for now

effects.log: You go back down the hill. The healer does not watch you go.

events.text: The healer-god listens to the light in you for a whole season and says it can be done, but slowly, and not cheaply: rare roots from three domains, a decade of needles of light, and patience you do not have yet.

choices.text: Stay the decade and learn patience

effects.log: A decade of needles and bitter dew. You learn a little patience, which surprises both of you.

choices.text: Pay for the rarest roots of three domains

effects.log: The roots cost a great deal. The healer says they are worth it, and does not smile.

choices.text: Leave, for now

effects.log: You go. The pulse the healer felt goes with you.

events.text: Everything is ready: the roots, the needles of light, the cold hall at the edge of the domain. The healer warns you plainly. The mending hurts more than the cracking did, and some gods stop it halfway.

choices.text: Do not stop it halfway

effects.log: Three days and three nights of the gods' kind of time. You do not stop it.

choices.text: Not yet. Not today

effects.log: The healer shrugs and covers the needles. They will be ready when you are.

events.text: The last step is the hardest, the healer says: the cracked centre is opened again with your own light, and you will have to find that light in the dark, where it went.

choices.text: Go into the dark and find it

effects.log: You find it, far down, a thread of warmth. You follow it back.

choices.text: Ask for more time

effects.log: The healer gives you time, as if it were a small thing.

events.text: You send word to {npc} by herald: a duel, at the hour the sun rises over the domains, on the old threshing floor of the gods, before witnesses. {He} sends back one word. Yes.

choices.text: Meet {him} at sunrise

ok.log: Before the sun is fully up, {npc} is on one knee and the witnesses are very quiet.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you hoped. The heralds will talk about it for a century.

choices.text: Send word that you have changed your mind

effects.log: You withdraw the challenge. Some of the witnesses laugh, quietly, and you hear them.

events.text: Your challenge reaches {npc} at a feast of the gods, read aloud by the herald so that the whole hall hears it. {He} puts down {his} cup and names the place: the bank of the river of stars, at noon.

choices.text: Go to the river of stars

ok.log: At noon the bank is yours, and {npc} is down among the reeds of light.

fail.log: At noon {npc} is the one standing. You walk home along the river of stars alone.

choices.text: Let noon pass

effects.log: Noon passes, and the feast talks about it.

events.text: You send {npc} a challenge with no limits written on it: a duel to the death, which the gods do not often ask of each other. Witnesses gather at an old shrine at the edge of the light. Only one of you is meant to walk away. {He} comes, and does not smile.

choices.text: Fight to the death

ok.log: The fight is long and silent. When it ends, {npc} is on the ground and cannot rise, and everyone waits to see what you will do.

fail.log: It goes the wrong way from the first exchange.

choices.text: Call it off before the first exchange

effects.log: You let your light fall before the first exchange. {npc} looks at you for a long time, and goes. The witnesses do not.

events.text: {npc} accepts your challenge to the death in a hand of gold on a tablet of cloud, and adds at the bottom that {his} domain is in order. The meeting is on a bare peak above the domains at dusk, with the wind of heaven against you both.

choices.text: Climb the peak

ok.log: At dusk, on the bare peak, {npc} falls, and stays down. The wind of heaven keeps blowing as if nothing had happened.

fail.log: On the bare peak, {npc} is the stronger.

choices.text: Send a tablet instead

effects.log: You send a tablet calling it off. {npc} reads it and breaks it, and tells every god what it said.

events.text: You find the god you remember on the steps of their domain, younger than they will be, laughing with their heralds. In the life you came back from, that laugh was the last thing you heard. They look at you and do not know you.

choices.text: Settle it, here and now

fail.log: It ends the way it ended before, almost. You get up. The god does not know what they just won.

choices.text: Let them go: this life is not that one

effects.log: You let them go. They never know how close it was.

events.text: The god you remember is alone in a garden of their pantheon, tending a tree of light. In another life they burned your temples. Here they have done nothing to you yet. Nobody would blame you either way.

events.text: A god you have never met waits for you at the border of the domain you took. "Its old god was my sworn friend," they say. "You took a throne. I am taking it out of you, one way or another."
